question: At a stop sign there is no stop line and no marked crosswalk. Where do you stop?
optionA: Just before the cross road, where you can see
optionB: Level with the sign post, wherever it stands
optionC: Partway into the cross road for a view
optionD: Behind the car already stopped at the sign
explanation: With no stop line or marked crosswalk, stop before entering the intersecting road, no more than 1.5 m back, where you can see approaching traffic. Stopping behind a car that is stopped at the sign does not count; you must stop again at the sign.

question: A red and white triangle points downward at the end of your road. What must you do?
explanation: That is a yield sign. Slow down and give the right of way to traffic in or close to the intersection, stopping only if you need to. A full stop every time is what a stop sign asks.

question: Which shape is used only for the stop sign?
explanation: The eight-sided octagon is used for stop signs and nothing else, so you can recognise it from behind or under snow. The five-sided pentagon is the school zone sign.

question: A sign shows a black symbol inside a green circle. What does the green circle mean?
optionB: The action is allowed at night
explanation: On regulatory signs a green circle gives permission for the action shown. A red circle with a slash through it takes permission away.

question: A sign shows a black symbol inside a red circle with a slash. What does it tell you?
optionA: The action shown is not allowed
optionC: The action is allowed with care
explanation: A red circle with a slash denies permission for whatever is shown inside it, such as a turn or a U-turn. A green circle would mean the action is allowed.

question: Most regulatory signs, other than stop and yield, are:
explanation: The most common regulatory signs are rectangular or square with a white background and black or red lettering or symbols. Yellow diamonds warn, orange marks work zones and green guides.

question: A white sign shows two cars side by side inside a green circle. It means:
explanation: Two cars in a green circle mean passing is permitted where it is safe. The same two cars in a red circle with a slash mean do not pass.

question: A white rectangular sign shows a red circle with a slash over a black U-shaped arrow. You may not:
optionD: Turn to go the opposite way
explanation: A crossed-out U-shaped arrow means no U-turn: you may not turn to go back the way you came. A crossed-out left arrow would mean no left turn.

question: At the end of a street you see a solid red disc crossed by one white bar. It tells you:
explanation: The red circle with a white bar is the do not enter sign, posted where traffic is coming toward you, such as the wrong end of a one-way street or an exit ramp.

question: A black-and-white sign shows an arrow with the words ONE WAY. It tells you that:
optionA: You must turn the way the arrow shows
optionB: Traffic moves only as the arrow shows
optionC: The lane ends in that direction
explanation: A one-way sign tells drivers that traffic may travel only in the direction of the arrow. It does not, by itself, require you to turn.

question: A sign beside a lane shows a white arrow curving right, with the word ONLY. Drivers in that lane must:
optionD: Yield to all drivers turning left
explanation: A right turn only lane sign means drivers in that lane must turn right at the intersection. A sign with a straight arrow and a curved arrow would allow both.

question: A lane sign shows one arrow pointing straight and one curving left. In that lane you may:
explanation: That sign marks a straight through or left turn only lane: you may go straight or turn left from it, but not turn right.

question: A sign at a traffic light reads NO RIGHT TURN ON RED. Facing a red light, you must:
optionA: Wait for a green light to turn right
optionB: Turn right after a full stop
optionC: Turn right only when no one is nearby
optionD: Turn right only from the left lane
explanation: Normally you may turn right on a red light after a full stop, unless a sign says no right turn on red. With that sign you wait for the green light.

question: A white sign shows a black arrow curving left with a red circle and slash over it. It means:
explanation: A crossed-out left-curving arrow means left turns are not permitted at that point. A crossed-out U-shaped arrow would mean no U-turn.

question: A white sign shows an arrow sloping down to the right of an island symbol. It tells you to:
explanation: The keep right sign means you must drive to the right of the traffic island or obstruction it is posted on. It is a regulatory sign, so it must be obeyed.

question: A white sign with the word MAXIMUM and a number shows:
optionA: The speed you must always drive
optionC: The speed for the next curve
optionD: The top speed in ideal conditions
explanation: A maximum speed sign gives the highest speed allowed under ideal conditions. Slow down below it in rain, snow, fog or heavy traffic; it is not a speed you must keep up.

question: A sign warns that the maximum speed changes a short way ahead. You should:
optionA: Get ready to adjust your speed
optionB: Speed up to reach the new limit
optionC: Keep the old limit for 1 km
optionD: Stop and check the new limit
explanation: A change in maximum speed ahead sign warns that a new speed limit starts shortly. Prepare to adjust your speed so you are at the new limit when you reach it.

question: A sign shows the letter P with a red circle and slash, and arrows pointing both ways. It means:
explanation: That is a no parking sign with arrows: parking is not allowed in either direction from the sign. A separate no stopping sign is stricter and bans even brief stops.

question: A sign says NO STOPPING. In that area you may:
optionA: Stop to drop off a passenger
optionC: Not stop, even for a moment
explanation: No stopping means you may not stop your vehicle there at all, except to obey a signal or police officer or to avoid a collision. Dropping off a passenger is still a stop.

question: A sign shows a wheelchair symbol over a parking space. Who may park there?
optionC: Any car after normal business hours
optionD: Vehicles with the permit or plate
explanation: The space is reserved for people with a mobility disability whose vehicle displays the special plate or permit, hung from the rearview mirror. There is no time or hours exception.

question: A white sign shows a truck with an arrow and the words TRUCK ROUTE. It means:
optionA: Trucks may go only as the arrow shows
optionB: No trucks are allowed on this road
optionC: Trucks must keep to the right-hand lane
optionD: Trucks may park along this road
explanation: A truck route sign tells truck traffic it may proceed only in the direction shown by the arrow or arrows. It does not ban cars or set lanes.

question: A sign shows a black arrow pointing straight up and another curving right, with no left arrow. At the intersection you may:
optionC: Go straight, or turn either way
explanation: That through or right turn only sign allows two movements: straight ahead or a right turn. A left turn is not shown, so it is not permitted from that lane.

question: A white crossbuck sign with a red border stands at a crossing. What is it marking?
explanation: The X-shaped crossbuck, white with a red reflective border, marks the railway crossing itself. It replaced the older crossbuck with Railway Crossing in black letters.

question: A small sign under a railway crossbuck shows a number. The number tells you:
optionA: How many trains pass through each day
optionB: How far ahead the tracks are
optionC: The speed limit at the tracks
optionD: How many tracks you will cross
explanation: A smaller sign below the crossbuck shows when there is more than one set of tracks to cross. After one train passes, check for another on the other tracks.

question: A crossbuck at a railway crossing also has a stop sign on its post. You must:
optionA: Make a full stop before crossing
optionB: Stop only if a train is in sight
optionC: Slow down and look both ways
optionD: Stop only when the gates drop
explanation: When a stop sign is posted at a railway crossing, you must come to a full stop before crossing, train or no train. Then look and listen before you go.

question: A regulatory sign and a police officer directing traffic tell you different things. You follow:
explanation: You must obey regulatory signs unless a peace officer directs you otherwise, so the officer's direction comes first. Following the driver ahead is never the rule.

question: A sign shows a pedestrian walking on a crosswalk. What is it showing you?
explanation: The pedestrian crosswalk sign marks the location of a crosswalk. Be ready to stop and yield to anyone crossing or about to cross.

question: A sign shows two children walking, posted at a crossing near a school. It marks:
explanation: The school crosswalk sign shows where children cross on their way to and from school. Watch for crossing guards and children who may step out.

question: A sign shows a crossed-out picture of litter being thrown. It means:
explanation: The do not litter sign is a regulatory sign: throwing litter from a vehicle is an offence. It says nothing about services.

question: A five-sided sign has a fluorescent yellow-green background and two children. It marks:
explanation: The five-sided fluorescent yellow-green sign with two school children is the school area sign. Slow to the school area limit posted with it whenever children are present.

question: Most warning signs in Nova Scotia are:
explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with black lettering or symbols on a yellow background. Orange signs mark work zones and green rectangles give directions.

question: A yellow diamond sign shows a red octagon symbol with an arrow. It warns of:
explanation: The stop sign ahead warning is posted where the stop sign itself is hard to see in time. Begin slowing so you can stop at the intersection.

question: A yellow diamond pictures a car trailing two S-shaped tire tracks. It warns that:
optionC: The road is slippery when wet
explanation: The slippery when wet sign warns that the surface loses grip in rain. Slow down, avoid sudden braking or steering, and leave more space.

question: A yellow diamond shows a traffic light symbol. It warns you that:
explanation: That sign gives advance warning of traffic signal lights, often where a curve or hill hides them. Be ready to stop if the light is red or turns yellow.

question: A yellow diamond shows a truck coming onto the road from the side. It warns of:
explanation: The truck entering sign warns that heavy trucks may pull onto the road from a side entrance. They are slow to speed up, so be ready to slow down.

question: A yellow diamond shows a fire truck. It means:
optionA: A fire hall is closed ahead
optionB: Fire trucks may enter the road
optionC: Do not park near the hydrant
optionD: Fire lane, no stopping at any time
explanation: The fire truck entrance sign warns that fire vehicles may come out of or turn into a station driveway ahead. Do not block the entrance.

question: A yellow diamond shows two lines that come closer together. It warns that:
explanation: The road narrows sign is often posted before a bridge. Hazard markers may show which side to keep to; slow down and stay in your lane.

question: A yellow diamond shows a side road meeting your road where your view is blocked. It warns of:
explanation: A hidden intersection sign means drivers at the side road ahead cannot see you well, and you cannot see them. Slow down and be ready to stop.

question: A yellow diamond shows a truck on a steep slope. It warns of:
explanation: The steep decline sign warns of a sharp downhill grade. You may need a lower gear to keep your speed under control without riding the brakes.

question: A yellow diamond shows a bump in the road. You should:
explanation: The bump or rough road sign warns of an uneven surface. Slow down to keep control and protect your vehicle; there is no need to stop.

question: A yellow diamond shows the ends of a median meeting into a single road. It warns that:
explanation: Divided highway ends means two-way traffic begins beyond this point, often confirmed by a two-way traffic sign. Keep right of the centre line.

question: A yellow diamond shows a road splitting around a median. It warns that:
explanation: The divided highway ahead sign marks the change from an undivided road to a divided one. Keep to the right of the median.

question: A yellow diamond shows a bridge that lifts. It warns of:
optionA: A bridge that opens for boats
optionD: A bridge with a steel deck
explanation: The bridge opening sign warns that the bridge ahead can be raised or swung open to let boats pass. Watch for signals and gates.

question: A yellow sign shows a curve to the right with a smaller speed tab under it. The speed shown is:
optionA: The new speed limit after it
optionB: A safe speed for that curve
optionC: A minimum speed for the curve
explanation: The tab under a curve sign gives a safe speed for that turn in good conditions. It does not change the speed limit on the road beyond.

question: A yellow diamond shows a narrow gap in the road such as a culvert or underpass. It warns of:
explanation: The narrow structure sign warns of a bridge, culvert, underpass or similar structure that is narrower than the road leading to it.

question: A yellow diamond shows the right lane line ending. It tells you that:
optionA: The right lane is for exits
optionB: The right lane is closed now
explanation: The right lane ends sign warns that the lane will finish shortly. Drivers in it should merge left when it is safe; others should let them in.

question: A sign shows a bent arrow on a black-and-white checkerboard border. It warns of:
optionA: A sharp turn in that direction
optionB: A dead end in that direction
optionD: A lane shift in a work zone
explanation: The checkerboard border is a warning to slow down, and the arrow shows the direction the road bends sharply.

question: A row of yellow signs with black arrowheads appears along the outside of a bend. These chevrons:
optionA: Mark the end of a passing lane
optionB: Guide you around a sharp curve
explanation: Chevron signs are posted in groups to guide drivers around sharp curves. Slow down before the curve and follow them through.

question: A yellow sign shows a height, such as 4.0 m, over a road symbol. It warns of:
optionA: A height limit for trucks only
explanation: The low clearance sign warns of an underpass or structure with the overhead clearance shown. Tall vehicles and loads must not go under it.

question: A yellow diamond shows two lines joining into one, with one line curving in. It means:
explanation: The merge sign warns that two lanes of traffic are about to join. Drivers on both roads share the duty to merge smoothly and safely.

question: At a merge sign, who is responsible for a smooth merge?
explanation: The handbook says drivers approaching from both lanes are equally responsible for seeing that traffic merges smoothly. Be ready to yield when you need to.

question: A hazard marker with black lines stands beside an obstacle. The handbook says if the lines slope to the right, you:
optionA: Drive to the left of it
optionB: Drive to the right of it
optionC: Drive on either side of it
explanation: Hazard markers show which side to pass on: if the black lines are sloped to the right, drive to the right of the sign; if sloped to the left, drive to the left.

question: A yellow diamond sign shows a road crossed by railway tracks. As you approach, you should:
optionA: Stop every time at the tracks, then go
optionB: Speed up to clear the tracks
optionC: Look, listen and be ready to stop
explanation: A yellow and black railway warning sign is posted before the crossing. Slow down, look both ways and listen, since you may have to stop.

question: A yellow diamond shows a moose. When are such animals most likely on the road?
explanation: Animal crossing signs mark known crossing areas for large animals like moose and deer. Watch most closely from dusk to dawn and use high beams when you can.

question: A diamond-shaped sign shows a child with a ball. It warns that:
explanation: The playground sign warns you are approaching a playground. Reduce speed and watch for children who may run into the road.

question: A sign reads TWO WAY TRAFFIC with arrows pointing up and down. It tells you that:
optionA: A second lane opens for you
optionC: You may pass on either side
optionD: The road becomes a one-way street
explanation: The two-way traffic sign reminds drivers that the road carries traffic in both directions, so the normal two-way rules apply. Keep to the right.

question: A yellow sign reads USE 4-WAY FLASHERS BELOW 70 KM/H on a hill with a climbing lane. You must turn on your flashers if:
optionA: You are passing in the left lane
explanation: Where posted on climbing lanes, vehicles that cannot keep above 70 km/h must use their four-way flashers to warn faster traffic coming up behind.

question: An orange triangle with a red border on the back of a farm tractor marks:
explanation: The slow-moving vehicle sign is required on farm tractors and any vehicle that cannot go faster than 40 km/h in normal conditions. Slow down when you see it.

question: You see a yellow warning sign for a hazard you do not recognise. The safest response is to:
optionA: Slow down and be ready to react
optionB: Keep your speed until you see it
explanation: Warning signs caution you about changing road conditions ahead. Even if you are unsure of the symbol, slowing down gives you time to react to what it warns of.

question: A yellow diamond shows a bicycle. It warns that:
optionB: Cyclists may be on the road
explanation: The bicycle sign warns of cyclists using or crossing the road. Give them room: when passing a cyclist, leave at least one metre.

question: Signs that mark construction and maintenance work zones are usually:
explanation: Work zones are marked with orange warning signs carrying black messages. When you see orange, go on high alert and follow the signs' directions.

question: A work zone sign shows the symbol of a person working. When is this kind of sign used?
optionA: Day and night until the work ends
optionB: Only while workers are on site
explanation: Human activity signs, those with a person symbol, are used only when the work site is active and people are at risk of being struck. Take extra care.

question: A worker holds a paddle showing STOP on one side and SLOW on the other. That worker is:
explanation: Traffic control persons use stop/slow paddles to direct traffic safely past a work site. You must obey their directions; failing to is an offence.

question: According to the handbook, the biggest cause of collisions in work zones is:
explanation: Speed variation between vehicles causes the most work zone collisions. Adjust your speed gradually so all traffic moves at the same reduced speed. Driver inattention is second.

question: A flashing light board in a work zone shows a single arrow pointing left. You should:
optionA: Pass it only on the left side
optionC: Stop and wait for a signal
optionD: Pass it only on the right side
explanation: A single arrow means the lane ahead is closed or blocked; it is safe to pass the board only on the side the arrow shows.

question: A flashing light board shows two arrowheads pointing in opposite directions. It means:
optionA: The road is closed both ways
optionB: You may pass on either side
optionC: You must stop and turn back
optionD: You must pass on the left
explanation: Two arrowheads displayed at the same time mean the lane ahead is blocked but it is safe to pass the board on either side.

question: A flashing light board shows its lamps in a straight bar, the caution mode. This tells you:
optionA: It is always safe to pass now
optionB: The work zone has now ended
optionC: Use caution; passing may not be safe
optionD: All lanes are closed to traffic ahead
explanation: Caution mode alerts you to a hazard, like a vehicle in the lane or workers placing signs. It does not mean it is safe to pass; you must judge the conditions yourself.

question: A work zone sign warns that the right lane will end ahead. When should you merge left?
optionB: Only when told by a worker
optionD: As soon as it is safe
explanation: Merge as soon as safely possible. Racing to the merge point in the closing lane and pushing in at the last moment causes collisions.

question: In a work zone, a DO NOT PASS sign is posted before a lane closure. This sign is:
optionA: Regulatory, so you must obey it
optionC: A guide to the next exit
optionD: In force only when workers are seen
explanation: Do Not Pass is a regulatory sign used to create an orderly flow before a merge point. Disobeying it is an offence that can bring a ticket.

question: An orange sign warns of tar sprayed on the road ahead. What risk does it point out?
explanation: Fresh tar can make the surface slippery, and tire spray can stick it to your paint. Choose another route or drive to avoid the hazard.

question: An orange sign warns of uneven lanes. The danger is that:
optionA: The road narrows to one lane
optionB: The road is closed at night
optionC: A tire can catch the lane edge
optionD: Water pools in the low lane
explanation: Uneven lanes means a difference in height between lanes. A tire catching that edge as you change lanes could make you lose control.

question: An orange sign warns of blasting ahead and asks you to turn off your radio transmitter. Why?
optionA: The noise will drown out radios
optionC: To keep your full attention on the road
optionD: Radio signals could set off charges
explanation: Radio transmitters can trigger electric blasting caps, so drivers are asked to shut them off in a blasting zone. Be ready to stop and watch for debris.

question: A green rectangular sign shows town names and distances. It is a:
explanation: Guide signs are rectangular, usually green with white letters, and give directions, route numbers and distances. Other colours guide you to services and attractions.

question: A route sign shows the number 102 in a highway shield. A 100-series highway in Nova Scotia is:
optionA: A road with no posted speed limit
explanation: The 100-series highways are provincial controlled-access highways, mostly divided, that you enter and leave only at interchanges.

question: You see someone driving dangerously through a work zone. The handbook says you should:
optionA: Follow them to get the plate
explanation: If you see someone driving irresponsibly through a work zone, report it to the police. Chasing or racing past them only adds risk.

question: You face a steady yellow light as you approach an intersection. You should:
optionA: Stop if you can do so safely
optionB: Speed up to clear the light
optionC: Stop even if you must skid
optionD: Treat it as a flashing yellow
explanation: A yellow light means stop before entering the intersection if you can stop safely. If you are too close to stop safely, go through with care; never speed up to beat the red.

question: The signal facing you is flashing red. What must you do?
optionA: Slow down and go with care
optionB: Stop, then go when it is safe
optionC: Stop and wait for a green light
explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop, and do not go until you can enter without interfering with other traffic.

question: A traffic light is flashing yellow. It means:
optionB: The light will soon turn red
optionC: Slow down and go with caution
explanation: A flashing yellow or amber light has the same meaning as a warning sign: slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop unless traffic requires it.

question: In Nova Scotia, a flashing green light facing you means you may:
optionC: Go only after coming to a full stop
optionD: Go straight or turn either way
explanation: Under the Using the Road Regulations, a driver facing a flashing green ball signal may proceed, whether going straight or turning. You must still yield to pedestrians and to vehicles already in the intersection.

question: The traffic lights at an intersection are not working at all. You should treat it as:
optionC: A green light for main roads
explanation: When signal lights are out, treat the intersection as a multi-stop: come to a full stop, then go when you have the right of way and it is safe.

question: You are stopped at a red light and want to turn right. There is no sign. You may:
optionB: Turn after stopping, if it is safe
optionC: Never turn until it is green
optionD: Turn only if a sign says you may do so
explanation: Unless a sign says no turn on red, you may turn right on a red light after stopping and making sure the way is clear of pedestrians and traffic.

question: When is a left turn on a red light allowed?
optionA: From any lane when it is clear
optionB: Any time after a full stop
optionC: From one one-way street to another
optionD: Only from a two-way street to a one-way
explanation: A left turn on red is illegal except from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after a full stop and when it is safe.

question: You face a green light and a green arrow pointing left. Turning left, you:
optionB: Must wait for the arrow to go
optionD: Follow the arrow and may turn
explanation: With a green arrow, turning traffic is controlled by the arrow, so you may turn in its direction. Through traffic follows the round green light.

question: A green turn arrow changes to a yellow arrow. You should:
optionA: Stop unless too close to stop safely
optionB: Finish the turn as quickly as you can
explanation: A yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending. Stop, unless you are too close to the intersection to stop safely; then go through with caution.

question: A light over your lane shows a red X. You must:
optionC: Use the lane to turn only
optionD: Use the lane with flashers on
explanation: Lane control signals are mounted over the lanes they control. Never drive in a lane under a red X, regardless of other signs or signals.

question: Your light turns green, but a pedestrian is still crossing in front of you. You must:
explanation: If a signal changes while a pedestrian is still in the street, you must allow the pedestrian to finish crossing safely. Green never lets you hit or crowd a pedestrian.

question: A pedestrian is crossing with the Walk signal. Compared with vehicles turning across the crosswalk, the pedestrian:
optionB: Must wait for cars to clear
optionC: Has the same rights as they do
optionD: Has the right of way over them
explanation: Pedestrians crossing with the Walk signal have the right of way, just as they do crossing with a green light, including over vehicles turning across their path.

question: Yellow pavement lines are used to divide:
explanation: Yellow lines separate travel lanes moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

question: What do white lane lines between lanes separate?
explanation: White lines separate travel lanes moving in the same direction and also mark the right edge of the road. Yellow lines separate opposing traffic.

question: The centre of a two-lane road is a broken yellow line. This means:
optionA: Passing is not allowed at all
optionC: Passing with care is allowed both ways
optionD: Passing is allowed in one direction only
explanation: A broken yellow centre line on a two-lane, two-way road means passing with care is permitted in both directions when it is safe.

question: The centre of the road is a double solid yellow line. To pass another car, you may:
optionA: Cross them whenever the way is clear
optionB: Cross them only to pass slow trucks
optionC: Cross them only in daylight hours
optionD: Not cross the lines in either direction
explanation: You may not drive left of a double solid yellow line to pass a car in either direction. The narrow exceptions are passing a cyclist with at least 1 m of room, or a slow vehicle that has pulled to the far right.

question: The centre lines are a solid yellow line on your side and a broken line on the other. You:
optionA: May not pass from your side
optionC: May pass only on the right
optionD: Must stay right of both lines
explanation: Passing with care is permitted only when the broken yellow line is on your side of the centre markings. With the solid line on your side, you may not pass.

question: You are on a divided highway and see a solid yellow line on your right and a white line on your left. This means:
optionA: You are in a passing lane
optionB: You are going the wrong way
optionC: You are on an exit ramp
optionD: The two lanes are about to merge
explanation: On a divided highway, white is the right-edge line and solid yellow is the left-edge line. If you see the reverse, you are travelling in the wrong direction.

question: A two-lane highway has an extra climbing lane going uphill. Slower traffic should:
explanation: On a climbing lane all traffic keeps to the right unless passing. Faster traffic passes in the left lane and returns right when done.

question: The climbing lane ends where the dividing line turns solid. As a driver passing on the left, you should:
optionA: Pass quickly before the lane ends
optionB: Force your way into the right lane
optionC: Stop until the right lane clears
optionD: Not start a pass at the solid line
explanation: Do not attempt to pass once you reach the solid line at the end of the climbing lane. The vehicle in the right lane has the right of way.

question: Wide lines painted where on-ramps and off-ramps meet a highway are called:
explanation: Continuity lines are wider than regular lane lines and separate the through lane from entry or exit ramps.

question: A centre lane is marked for two-way left turns. You may use it to:
explanation: A two-way left-turn lane is shared by both directions for left turns only. Never use it to pass, and do not drive in it for a long distance.

question: When using a two-way left-turn lane, you should enter it:
optionC: Close to where you will turn
explanation: Move into the two-way left-turn lane as close to your turning point as possible, stop near where you will turn and yield to approaching traffic.

question: Your side of the road has two or more marked lanes going your way. May you cross the centre line to pass?
optionA: Yes, if the centre line is broken
optionB: Yes, when the right lane is full
optionC: Yes, if oncoming traffic is clear
optionD: No, pass using your own lanes
explanation: Where there are two or more traffic lanes in your direction, driving left of the centre line to pass is prohibited. Pass in the lanes going your way.

question: A pedestrian is crossing at an intersection with no painted crosswalk lines. The pedestrian:
explanation: Every intersection has a crosswalk, even when it is unmarked. At an intersection without signals, pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk have the right of way.

question: What is the minimum age to apply for a Nova Scotia learner's licence (Class 7)?
explanation: You must be at least 16 to apply for a Class 7 learner's licence. If you are 16 or 17, you also need the written consent of a parent or guardian.

question: A 17-year-old applying for a learner's licence also needs:
explanation: Applicants under 18 need written parental or guardian consent. A driver training course is optional for a learner and only shortens the wait for the road test.

question: How many questions must you answer correctly on each part of the Class 7 knowledge test?
explanation: The test has a rules of the road part and a road sign part, each 20 multiple-choice questions, and you must get at least 16 right on each (80 percent).

question: While driving on a learner's licence, who must be in the front passenger seat?
optionA: Any adult with a driver's licence
optionB: A parent, whatever licence they hold
explanation: A learner must drive with a supervising driver in the front seat who holds a valid regular licence and is not in the graduated licensing program. Age alone does not qualify someone.

question: Apart from the supervising driver, how many passengers may a learner carry in normal driving?
optionD: As many as there are belts
explanation: A learner may carry no passengers other than the supervising driver. The exceptions are road test examiners and up to three students with an approved instructor in a dual-brake car.

question: What blood-alcohol level is allowed for a driver with a learner's licence?
explanation: Learners, and newly licensed drivers, must have a blood-alcohol level of zero while driving. Any alcohol detected brings a suspension.

question: How long is a Nova Scotia learner's licence valid?
explanation: A learner's licence issued since April 1, 2015 is valid for 2 years. You must pass the road test before it expires or redo the knowledge tests.

question: Without a driver education course, how long must you hold a learner's licence before the road test?
explanation: Learners usually wait at least 12 full months before the road test. An approved driver education course shortens the wait to 9 months.

question: Completing an approved driver education course as a learner lets you:
optionA: Take the road test after 9 months
optionB: Skip the road test for the 5N stage
explanation: An approved course, at least 25 hours of classroom and 10 hours of in-car instruction, cuts the waiting time for the road test from 12 to 9 months. It does not lift any learner restriction.

question: As a learner, how many demerit points lead to a six-month suspension?
explanation: A Class 7 learner is suspended for six months at 4 demerit points. Newly licensed drivers are suspended at 6 points and fully licensed drivers at 10.

question: After you pass the road test, you move to which licence stage?
explanation: Passing the road test moves you from the learner stage to the newly licensed stage, Class 5N, where you stay for at least two years.

question: A newly licensed (Class 5N) driver may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m. unless they:
optionA: Are driving only on a 100-series highway
optionB: Have only one passenger with them
optionC: Are 19 years of age or older
optionD: Have a supervising driver or exemption
explanation: Class 5N drivers may not drive from midnight to 5 a.m. unless a supervising driver is in the front seat with no other passenger, or they carry written Registrar authorization to drive alone for work, school or volunteer firefighting.

question: How many passengers may a Class 5N driver carry in the front seat?
explanation: A newly licensed driver may carry only one passenger in the front seat, and no more rear-seat passengers than there are seat belts.

question: How many demerit points bring a six-month suspension for a newly licensed (Class 5N) driver?
explanation: A Class 5N driver can be called to a meeting with the Registrar or sent to a driver improvement program at 4 points, and is suspended for six months at 6 points.

question: For a fully licensed driver outside the graduated program, a suspension comes at:
explanation: A fully licensed driver can be called to a meeting with the Registrar or sent to a driver improvement program at 6 points, and is suspended for six months at 10 points.

question: How long do demerit points stay on your Nova Scotia driving record?
explanation: Demerit points are removed from your driving record 24 months after the date of the conviction they were assigned for.

question: For 2 years after leaving the newly licensed stage, a driver is still a novice driver. During those 2 years they:
optionA: Must have zero alcohol or drugs
explanation: Novice drivers, including fully licensed drivers in their first 2 years after the newly licensed stage, must have no alcohol or drugs in their body while driving and may not act as a supervising driver.

question: What must a newly licensed driver complete, besides two years in the stage, to move on?
optionA: A second road test with an examiner
explanation: To leave the newly licensed stage you need at least two full years at that stage and a completed approved driver training course, with the certificate given to the Registry.

question: Using a hand-held cell phone to talk or text while driving in Nova Scotia is:
optionA: Legal with one hand on the wheel
explanation: Nova Scotia law bans using a hand-held phone to talk or text while driving. Pull over and stop safely before using one.

question: Which statement about getting a learner's licence is correct?
optionC: You must take a road test
optionD: You must pass a vision test
explanation: Besides the two knowledge test parts, you must pass a vision test, prove your identity and age and pay the licence fee. Owning a car or insurance is not required.

question: Two vehicles stop at an all-way stop at about the same time, on roads that cross. Who must yield?
explanation: When two drivers reach a stop-controlled intersection at about the same time from crossing roads, the driver to the immediate left must yield, so the vehicle on the right goes first.

question: You are about to enter an intersection, and another car is already in it. Who has the right of way?
optionA: You, if you are on the right
explanation: A vehicle already in the intersection has the right of way over any vehicle that has not yet entered it.

question: You want to turn left at a green light, and an oncoming car is going straight. You must:
optionA: Turn first, since you are first
explanation: A driver turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians in the path, then turn when it is safe.

question: While you wait in the intersection to turn left, your front wheels should be:
explanation: Keep your wheels straight until you can complete the turn. If you are hit from behind with wheels turned left, you could be pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: You leave a private driveway onto a street. You must:
optionA: Stop and yield to all traffic
optionB: Yield only to vehicles on your left
explanation: When leaving a private driveway or parking lot, stop and yield to all vehicles and pedestrians. In a business or residential district, stop before crossing the sidewalk.

question: A car in the next lane has stopped at a crosswalk. Before you go past it, you must:
optionA: Sound your horn to warn walkers
optionB: Yield to anyone in the crosswalk
optionC: Speed up to clear the crosswalk
explanation: When a vehicle has stopped at a crosswalk, you may not overtake it unless you yield to any pedestrian in the crosswalk. The stopped car may hide someone stepping into your lane, so slow down and be ready to stop.

question: An ambulance with lights and siren is coming up behind you. You must:
optionC: Pull to the right and stop
explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches from ahead or behind, move to the right edge or curb and stop until it has passed or a peace officer tells you to move.

question: How close may you follow a fire department vehicle answering an alarm?
explanation: Never follow a fire vehicle responding to an emergency within 150 metres, and never overtake an emergency vehicle with its lights and siren on.

question: A police car with flashing lights is stopped on the shoulder of a two-lane road posted at 80 km/h. You must:
optionA: Slow to 60 km/h as you pass
optionD: Slow to 30 km/h as you pass
explanation: When passing a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing, slow down to 60 km/h, or the posted limit if it is lower. On multi-lane roads, also move over a lane if it is safe.

question: On a four-lane highway, a tow truck with flashing lights is stopped on the right shoulder at a collision. You should:
optionB: Slow down and move left if safe
explanation: Tow trucks at a collision are covered by the slow down, move over rule: slow to 60 km/h or less and move into a lane farther away if it is safe to do so.

question: You drive past a stopped police car with flashing lights, but it is across the median on a divided highway. You:
optionA: Must slow to 60 km/h as you pass
optionC: Need not slow down or move over
optionD: Must move to the far lane
explanation: The slow down, move over rule does not apply when the emergency vehicle is on the other side of the median of a divided highway.

question: A firefighter's hose lies across the road. You may drive over it:
optionA: If you go slowly over it
optionC: If there is no other route you can take
optionD: Only when a fire official directs you
explanation: Never drive over an unprotected fire hose unless a fire official directs you to. Driving over it can damage the hose and cut off water.

question: A transit bus is stopped on a street posted at 50 km/h and is signalling to pull out. You are behind it. You should:
optionA: Yield and let it pull out
explanation: Where the speed limit is 60 km/h or less, you must yield to a stopped transit bus signalling to re-enter traffic when you approach from behind and it is safe. This does not apply to school buses.

question: A school bus ahead has its red lights flashing and its stop arm out. On a two-lane road, you must:
optionC: Stop only if behind the bus
optionD: Stop only if children are seen
explanation: When a school bus shows flashing red lights, all drivers coming from behind or toward it must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing.

question: A school bus ahead turns on its flashing amber lights. This means the bus:
explanation: Flashing amber lights warn that the bus is about to stop. Passing is still allowed with extra caution, but be ready to stop for the red lights.

question: A crossing guard holds up a stop paddle at a school crosswalk. You must:
optionA: Slow and pass behind the children
optionB: Stop only if children are in your lane
optionC: Yield, then go when you can
optionD: Stop and stay stopped while it is up
explanation: Drivers must obey crossing guards. Stop before the crosswalk and remain stopped as long as the stop paddle is displayed.

question: The lights at a railway crossing start flashing as you approach. You must:
optionA: Stop and wait until it is safe
optionD: Stop on the tracks to look both ways
explanation: Flashing red lights at a crossbuck mean you must stop, just as for any flashing red signal, and go only when it is safe. Never try to beat a train.

question: You are already on the tracks when the crossing lights start flashing. You should:
explanation: If the lights start flashing or the gates begin to lower while you are crossing, keep moving. The signals allow time to clear, and the far gate will not trap you.

question: A train has just passed a multi-track crossing and the gates are still up. Before you go, you should:
optionD: Wait for a signal from the train
explanation: Do not move immediately after a train passes. First make sure another train is not coming, especially where more than one track crosses the road.

question: Your engine dies while you are on a level crossing. What is your first job?
optionA: Try to restart it several times
optionB: Wait in the car for help
optionC: Push it off with everyone inside
explanation: Immediately move everyone out of the vehicle and well away from the tracks, then post lookouts. Try to push or restart it only if no train is in sight; trains may need over a kilometre to stop.

question: Unless a sign says otherwise, the maximum speed on a Nova Scotia highway outside towns is:
explanation: Unless otherwise posted, the maximum speed on any highway in Nova Scotia is 80 km/h. Higher limits, such as 100 or 110 km/h on 100-series highways, must be posted.

question: Unless another limit is posted, the speed limit in an urban area lined with homes and businesses is:
explanation: Where no speed limit sign is posted, the limit is 50 km/h in an urban area (homes and businesses fronting the road for 100 m or more) and in public parks, and 80 km/h elsewhere.

question: A school area sign carries a tab reading MAXIMUM 30 km/h WHEN CHILDREN PRESENT. When does the 30 km/h limit apply?
optionB: Only on weekdays, September to June
optionC: When a child is outside near the road
optionD: At all times, day and night
explanation: The posted school area limit applies only when a child is present: outdoors on that road or on land within 30 m of its centre line. It does not depend on the clock or the calendar.

question: You pass an END SCHOOL AREA sign with no speed sign under it. Your speed limit is now:
optionA: 50 km/h until the next speed sign
optionB: 30 km/h until the next speed sign
optionD: The limit from before the school area
explanation: The end school area sign means the speed limit that applied just before the school area starts again. If a different limit follows, a maximum speed sign is posted with it.

question: A crossing has a railway crossbuck and a stop sign. How close to the nearest rail may you stop?
explanation: Where you must stop at a railway crossing, such as one with a stop sign or flashing signals, stop no closer than 5 metres from the nearest rail, then go only when it is safe.

question: The two-second rule helps you judge:
optionA: How long to signal a turn
optionC: When to brake for a light
optionD: How long to stop at a sign
explanation: Pick a fixed point ahead; when the vehicle ahead passes it, count two seconds. If you reach the point first, you are following too closely.

question: On a wet road in rain, your following distance should be at least:
explanation: In rain, the handbook says to increase your normal following distance to four or more seconds, since wet pavement can make stopping distances two to ten times longer.

question: In ideal conditions at 80 km/h, about how far does a car need to stop completely?
explanation: At 80 km/h the handbook gives 56 metres of reaction distance plus 84 metres of braking, about 140 metres in total, even in ideal conditions.

question: Stopping distance gets longer at higher speed because:
explanation: At higher speed you cover more ground during your reaction time, and braking distance grows faster still, so total stopping distance rises sharply.

question: You should allow more following distance than usual when following:
explanation: Leave extra room behind a motorcycle, which can stop more quickly than a car, as well as behind large trucks and in poor conditions.

question: On a multi-lane highway, you are driving at the speed limit in the left lane. You should:
optionA: Stay left, you are at the limit
optionB: Speed up to stay in that lane
optionC: Move right once you have passed
explanation: The left lane is for passing. Driving at the limit does not entitle you to camp there; keep right unless passing, or others may try to pass you on the right.

question: Driving far below the limit on a clear highway can be dangerous because:
optionA: It wastes fuel and wears the brakes
optionD: Faster traffic may crash into you
explanation: A vehicle moving well below the normal speed is more likely to be in a crash, especially just over a hill or round a curve. A slow driver should pull over safely to let traffic pass.

question: On a two-lane road, you may move left of the centre line to pass only when:
optionA: You can see far enough ahead to pass safely
optionB: The car ahead is going under the speed limit
optionC: The driver ahead waves you past with a hand
optionD: You can finish the pass within ten seconds
explanation: To pass across the centre line, your view must be clear far enough that no oncoming traffic is affected, visibility must not be cut by fog, rain or snow, and the markings must allow it. Never pass on a hill or curve you cannot see over or around.

question: You are passing another car on a two-lane road. When is it safe to return to the right lane?
optionA: As soon as your front bumper is past it
optionB: When its headlights show in your mirror
optionD: After you count to two seconds
explanation: Signal right, check over your right shoulder, and move back when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: Another driver is passing you on a two-lane road. You should:
optionA: Speed up to help them pass
optionB: Brake hard to let them in
optionC: Keep right and not speed up
explanation: The driver being passed must help the other driver pass by keeping to the right and must not increase speed until the pass is complete.

question: A car ahead has started to pass a slow truck on a two-lane road. You should:
optionA: Follow it closely past the truck
optionB: Pass both of them at once
optionC: Sound your horn to hurry it
explanation: Where there are only two lanes, never follow another vehicle that has already begun to pass. Wait until the first vehicle has finished, then judge your own pass.

question: You are passing another vehicle at night. Your headlights should be:
optionA: On low beam until you pass
optionB: On high beam the whole time
explanation: When passing at night, use low-beam headlights until you have completed the pass so you do not dazzle the driver you are passing.

question: In which case does Nova Scotia law let you overtake a vehicle on its right?
optionA: When it is slower than you
explanation: You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is making a left turn and there is room without leaving the roadway. On multi-lane highways you may also pass on either side; the shoulder is never a passing lane.

question: You need to change lanes on a multi-lane road. Which step is part of a safe lane change?
explanation: Check your mirrors, signal, check your blind spot with a shoulder check, then steer gradually into the new lane while keeping your speed.

question: Before turning right, you should position your vehicle:
optionA: In the centre of the lane
explanation: Stay close to the right-hand edge of the road for a right turn so another vehicle cannot squeeze in between you and the curb. Yield to pedestrians in your path.

question: You start a turn in the right lane of two turning lanes. You should finish the turn in:
explanation: If there are two turning lanes, stay in your lane from start to finish: begin in the right turning lane and you enter the right receiving lane.

question: You are entering a 100-series highway from an on-ramp. You should:
optionA: Stop at the end of the ramp
explanation: Use the acceleration lane to bring your speed up to that of highway traffic, then merge into a safe gap. Highway traffic has the right of way.

question: Leaving a controlled-access highway, you should:
optionA: Slow down before the exit lane
optionC: Slow down in the exit lane
explanation: Signal well ahead, move into the deceleration lane without slowing down, then slow to the posted ramp speed there.

question: On a long highway trip, the handbook advises stopping for a rest at least every:
explanation: Stop at rest areas frequently, preferably at least once every 150 to 200 km, and take short walking breaks to stay alert.

question: You need to back up. Which way should you look?
optionA: Over your shoulder, out the back
optionD: Ahead, then reverse quickly by feel
explanation: Turn your body and look back over your right shoulder, with one hand at the top of the wheel, and back slowly while scanning in all directions.

question: You are entering a roundabout. Who has the right of way?
explanation: Vehicles entering a roundabout or rotary must yield to traffic already circulating. Drivers in the circle have the right of way over entering traffic.

question: In a roundabout, traffic travels around the central island:
explanation: All vehicles travel to the right around the central island, counterclockwise, until they reach their exit.

question: In a two-lane roundabout, you may exit:
optionD: From the lane you entered from
explanation: Move safely into the correct lane before your exit, signal right and leave from the outside lane. Never exit a roundabout or rotary from an inside lane.

question: When passing a cyclist, Nova Scotia law requires you to leave at least:
explanation: Drivers must leave at least one metre when passing a bicycle, including one riding in an unprotected bike lane. More room is safer at higher speeds.

question: You pass a cyclist and then want to turn right just ahead. The danger is called a:
explanation: A right hook happens when a driver passes a cyclist and turns right across the bike's path. If you cannot pass well before the turn, slow down and turn behind the cyclist.

question: Before opening your door after parking on a street, you should:
optionA: Open it slowly and lean out
optionD: Open it quickly, then close it
explanation: Stop, look, open, close: make sure it is safe and clear before opening a door, and do not leave it open longer than needed. A door opened into a cyclist can cause a serious crash.

question: A motorcyclist is riding ahead of you in your lane. The motorcyclist is entitled to:
optionB: The right edge of the lane
optionC: The full width of the lane
explanation: A motorcycle is entitled to a full lane. Do not share the lane with it, and allow extra following space.

question: You are behind a large truck and cannot see its driver in the truck's side mirror. This means:
optionB: You are at a safe distance
optionC: You may pass on the right
explanation: If you cannot see the truck driver in the side mirror, the trucker cannot see you. Trucks have large blind spots ahead, beside and up to about 60 metres behind.

question: Travelling above 60 km/h, a commercial truck may not follow another vehicle closer than:
explanation: Except when passing, the driver of a commercial vehicle travelling faster than 60 km/h must not follow another vehicle more closely than 60 metres.

question: Who must wear a seat belt where one is available?
explanation: The driver and every passenger must wear a seat belt, or for young children the right child seat. The driver is responsible for passengers under 16.

question: Your 14-year-old cousin rides with you and will not buckle up. Who is legally responsible?
explanation: The driver is responsible for ensuring every passenger under 16 is properly belted or in the right child restraint.

question: Under current Nova Scotia rules, a young child must ride in a rear-facing seat until at least age:
explanation: Under the Traffic Safety Act rules in force since October 2026, children stay rear-facing until at least age 2, and in a five-point harness seat until at least age 4.

question: A rear-facing child seat must never be placed:
optionA: In front of an active airbag
explanation: A rear-facing child seat must not be used in a seat with an active frontal airbag: a deploying airbag strikes it with too much force. The back seat is the safest place for children.

question: You are parking on a street. You must not park within how many metres of a fire hydrant?
explanation: You must not stop or park within 5 metres of a fire hydrant or of a fire station driveway. Check local signs, as by-laws can add limits.

question: You must not park within how many metres of the nearest rail of a railway crossing?
explanation: You must not stop or park within 15 metres of the nearest rail of a railway crossing.

question: Parking beside a vehicle already parked at the curb is called:
explanation: Stopping or parking on the roadway side of a stopped or parked vehicle is double parking and is not allowed.

question: You park facing downhill next to a curb. Turn your front wheels:
optionA: Toward the curb, to the right
optionB: Away from the curb, to the left
optionD: Either way with the brake on
explanation: Facing downhill, with or without a curb, turn your wheels to the right so the car would roll into the curb or off the road, not into traffic. Then set the parking brake.

question: Your car is parked nose-up on a hill beside a curb. Your front wheels should point:
optionA: Toward the curb, to the right
optionB: Away from the curb, to the left
optionD: Either way, if the brake is set
explanation: Facing uphill with a curb, turn your wheels to the left so that if the car rolls back, the rear of the front tire catches the curb. Uphill with no curb, turn them right.

question: Whenever you leave your vehicle parked and unattended, you must:
optionB: Leave the keys under the driver's seat
optionC: Set the brake and stop the engine
optionD: Turn the wheels to the left
explanation: Whenever a vehicle is left standing unattended, apply the parking brake and turn off the engine. Take the key and lock the vehicle.

question: You are walking along a highway with no sidewalk. You should walk:
optionC: In the middle of the lane
explanation: Pedestrians on a highway without a sidewalk should walk facing traffic so they can see vehicles coming, and wear reflective or light clothing after dark.

question: At night a car is coming toward you. Your high beams must be off once it is within:
explanation: By law you must dim your headlights within 150 metres of an approaching vehicle and within 60 metres when following another vehicle.

question: You are following another vehicle at night. You must dim your headlights within:
explanation: Dim to low beam within 60 metres when following a vehicle, and within 150 metres of an oncoming one, so you do not dazzle the other driver.

question: Headlights must be turned on starting from:
explanation: Low beams and tail lights are required at nighttime, from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise, and whenever fog, rain, snow or poor light limits visibility.

question: Driving in fog or heavy snow, you should use:
explanation: Use low beams in rain, snow and fog. High beams reflect off the precipitation and make it harder to see; parking lights alone are not allowed while driving.

question: When are roads most slippery during a rain?
optionD: Only when rain turns to snow
explanation: Roads are most dangerous in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain, when oil and residue on the pavement mix with water to form a slick film.

question: Your tires may ride up on a film of water and lose grip. This is called:
explanation: Hydroplaning can begin around 55 km/h in a passenger car and may be total by about 85 km/h, leaving no grip to brake, steer or accelerate. Slow down on wet roads.

question: Which part of a road usually freezes first in cold weather?
explanation: Bridges, overpasses and shaded sections freeze before the rest of the road and stay icy longer. Black ice there is hard to see.

question: A tire suddenly blows out while you are driving. You should:
optionC: Shift into neutral and brake hard
optionD: Hold the wheel, ease off the gas
explanation: After a blowout, do not brake. Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease your foot off the accelerator slowly and steer to a safe stop off the highway.

question: Your brake pedal suddenly sinks and the car will not slow. First you should:
explanation: Pump the brake pedal several times to build hydraulic pressure. If that fails, apply the parking brake gently but firmly while holding the release button.

question: Your vehicle catches fire. After stopping and turning off the ignition, everyone should move at least:
explanation: Get passengers out and move at least 30 metres from the vehicle. Fight the fire only with an extinguisher and only if it is safe; never use water on a fuel fire.

question: A power line has fallen on your car after a crash. If there is no fire, you should:
optionD: Touch the frame to test it
explanation: Stay in the vehicle if at all possible. If you must leave because of fire, jump clear with feet together and shuffle at least 20 metres away.

question: On a rural road your right tires slip off the edge of the asphalt onto soft gravel. You should:
optionA: Brake hard and jerk back on
optionB: Speed up to climb back on
optionD: Ease off and steer back gently
explanation: Resist the urge to whip the car back onto the pavement. When the steering is under control, ease the wheels smoothly back on while looking at the centre of your lane.

question: You are involved in a collision. What must you do first?
explanation: A driver involved in a collision must stop immediately and stay at the scene; leaving is an offence. Help anyone injured and, on request, show your licence, vehicle documents and proof of insurance.

question: You hit a parked car and cannot find its owner. You must:
optionA: Leave a note, then nothing more
optionB: Leave a note and report it to police
optionD: Report it only if damage is large
explanation: Try to find and tell the owner. If you cannot, leave a written notice on the vehicle saying how to reach you, and report the collision to the police within 24 hours.

question: After drinking, what lowers your blood-alcohol level?
explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate, so only time lowers your blood-alcohol level. Coffee, cold showers and exercise do not make you sober.
